before.text: Agent-plugin version resolution never fails the marker: the scan of the plugin caches under the user profile (.codex/plugins/cache, .claude/plugins/cache, .grok/installed-plugins) skips any directory it cannot traverse (a link or other reparse point, an untrusted mount point, an inaccessible folder); a version file (.version or a plugin manifest) that exists but cannot be read (an IO or access error) yields no version, so resolution goes on to the next file and the next candidate; and resolution falls back to the synced plugin version when nothing yields one. Any other error still propagates. Unit tests take every plugin-version input (the agent plugin-root environment variables, the workspace sibling plugin folder and the user profile caches) from test-owned data, never from the process environment, the machine or the real profile, and a full unit run under a hostile environment (every plugin-root variable and HOME pointed at scripted bad data) stays 0 failed (operator 2026-10-20: "Fix scans in PR 87 (Recommended)", "Fold R3-P3 in first" and "Structural fix, round 4 (Recommended)"; IMPL-UNITGREEN-001, triage-report-b0e41c36f93c4c91b1bf2524eb579ef8).

before.text: The agent-history scan under ~ (.grok, .claude, .codex, .cursor) skips any directory it cannot traverse (a link or other reparse point, an untrusted mount point, an inaccessible folder) and never fails a submit or an import; when nothing usable is found the turn keeps None. Tests that submit imports read the real home, so they are integration tests (operator 2026-10-20: "Fix scans in PR 87 (Recommended)"; IMPL-UNITGREEN-001, triage-report-b0e41c36f93c4c91b1bf2524eb579ef8).
